title: How Netflix Never Buffers: CDNs Explained in 60 Seconds 🍿 #shorts
description:
Netflix doesn't stream every show from one far-away data centre. It keeps copies on servers close to you, often inside your internet provider's network: a content delivery network. Each show is also split into small chunks at several qualities, and your player picks the best quality your connection can handle right now and downloads a few chunks ahead, so the video keeps playing smoothly.

#Netflix #CDN #SystemDesign #Streaming #Backend #TechExplained #shorts

lines: Millions of people press play at the same time, and the video starts almost instantly.
If every stream came from one data centre far away, the video would travel thousands of kilometres, and it would stall.
So Netflix keeps copies of shows on servers close to you, often inside your own internet provider. That's a CDN.
Each show is cut into small chunks, stored at several qualities, from low to 4K.
Your player measures your speed and picks the best quality you can handle right now, downloading a few chunks ahead. Slow Wi-Fi? It quietly steps down instead of freezing.
Copies nearby. Small chunks. Smart quality.
